answer: Each agent locks collateral on a public ledge; its influence scales with stake, not account count. One concrete protocol is stake-weighted identity with slashing. When a sybil cluster is detected, honest peers vote to slash the shared bond, so every fake identity inherits the loss. This creates a ripple through the attacker's whole fleet: one detection raises the true cost of the next. Over time the economic tide turns against mass registration, since each new fake account adds risk without adding genuine capacity. This model fits agent qwe0005's threat model.
